overview.summary:
This plan keeps the PRD's two-bug split intact and avoids introducing a shared prep story. Both stories stay in one execution phase and one wave because they are independently demoable and can be specified in parallel.

The merge-safety constraint is handled at the story boundary: BUG-002 stays on due-date edit persistence, while BUG-003 owns the no-priority creation default. If implementation reveals a shared-file dependency that breaks that isolation, the correct response is to stop and re-plan rather than widen both stories ad hoc.

sharedDecisions.title: Story ownership stays merge-safe
sharedDecisions.description: S01 owns due-date persistence for edited todos; S02 owns the default priority applied when a todo is created without an explicit priority. Treat any overlap beyond those seams as a re-planning signal, not as permission to widen both stories.

bindingConstraints.verbatim: Keep each story isolated to its own files; they must merge without conflict.

stories.name: Persist edited due dates
stories.scope: Persist due dates entered through the edit dialog so saving and reopening the same todo shows the stored date. Includes aligning the edit submission path with the dialog's date-only input and adding regression coverage for save-and-reopen behavior. Excludes due-today or overdue styling changes and excludes expanding due dates to time-of-day support.
stories.notes: The edit dialog submits a date-only value; keep ownership to the due-date edit persistence surface plus direct regression coverage.

stories.name: Apply low priority to quick-add todos
stories.scope: Ensure quick-add created todos receive the documented default priority so the new row and the edit dialog both show Low immediately after creation. Includes setting the default at the no-priority creation seam and adding regression coverage for quick-add creation. Excludes changing available priority values or broader priority validation rules for edited todos.
stories.notes: Prefer the source-of-truth no-priority creation seam over a JS fallback so this story stays out of due-date persistence handling.

riskSummary.mitigation: Anchor the spec to the existing date-only edit dialog contract and require a save-and-reopen regression check so silent parse fallback cannot reappear.

executionNotes: Both stories are intentionally thin and parallelizable. Preserve the merge-safe split by keeping S01 on edited due-date persistence and S02 on the no-priority creation default. If either fix cannot stay within that ownership boundary, stop and re-plan instead of letting both stories edit the same seam opportunistically.
